newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver down on weak trends, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver down on weak trends, gold steady.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closed 10 rupees lower at 7,650 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,660 rupees amid sluggish industrial buying and weak trends in the world market. Silver was up by 15 rupees per kg on Monday.
** Gold 24 carat closed at the steady level of 4,950 rupees per 10 grammes amid limited activity during the day while inflow was scattered. Gold was down by 25 rupees per 10 grammes on Monday.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) closed steady at 58,000 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Monday. But they were up 1,200 rupees each last week.
Silver (.999) closed 10 rupees lower at 7,650 rupees per kg amid sluggish industrial buying, dealers said on Monday.

Silver was up by 15 rupees per kg. Silver however opened 20 rupees lower at 7,640 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,660 rupees but restricted arrivals and shortage of ready stock trimmed some of the early losses towards the close.
Sentiment at the close remained subdued, following trends in the world market. Silver was up by 95 rupees per kg last week.
Gold 24 carat closed at the steady level of 4,950 rupees per 10 grammes in restricted activity. Gold was down by 25 rupees per 10 grammes on Monday.

Gold opened at the steady level of 4,950 rupees and hovered there amid sluggish seasonal enquiries while restricted arrivals and narrow fluctuations in the world market kept local prices around previous closing level.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed steady at 58,000 rupees per piece. They were down by 200 rupees per piece on Monday but were up 1,200 rupees each last week.
Sentiment at the close however remained subdued as some traders expected the customs department in Bombay to resume the sale of confiscated gold.
